## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
**CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED.** The effluent pump is operating at 22.2% of its rated load (1.6A measured vs. 7.2A nameplate), indicating no hydraulic load. The pump is running but not moving fluid. This is a confirmed failure mode requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components are in good condition, but the pump failure prevents proper treatment unit operation and poses a risk of motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches and represents 22.9% of the total tank volume, which is within the normal operating range. No pumping is required at this time based on solids accumulation alone.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank | Good | Concrete, 1250-gallon capacity |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Light soiling; cleaned and reseated during this visit |
| Effluent Pump | **CRITICAL** | Running at no load; impeller failure, dry run, or severed discharge line indicated |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals observed |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no breakout or ponding observed |

## PUMP FAILURE ANALYSIS
The effluent pump is drawing 1.6 amps during operation. The manufacturer nameplate rating is 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load condition is classified as **CRITICAL -- No Load**. The pump motor is running but receiving no hydraulic resistance, which indicates one or more of the following:

- The impeller is broken or missing
- The discharge line is severed, disconnected, or blocked
- The pump is running dry (no fluid in the suction line)

Without fluid circulation through the pump, the aerobic treatment unit cannot receive effluent from the septic tank, and treatment cannot occur. Additionally, a motor running without load and without fluid cooling will overheat and fail rapidly.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED:**

1. **Immediate professional attention:** The effluent pump is operating at no load and must be inspected and repaired or replaced without delay. Do not continue to operate the system in this condition. A qualified service technician must inspect the pump, impeller, discharge line and all connections to identify the cause of the no-load condition and restore proper fluid circulation.

**SECONDARY (after pump is restored):**

2. Continue the 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is repaired and normal operation is confirmed.

3. Recommend measuring dissolved oxygen in the aerobic treatment unit at the next maintenance visit to establish a treatment baseline and confirm that the unit is processing effluent properly after pump repair.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Immediate Steps
Your aerobic treatment system cannot function without the effluent pump. The pump is currently running but not moving water. This is a critical failure. Do not delay in contacting a service technician. Continued operation without repair will damage the pump motor and may allow untreated effluent to back up into your home.

### After Repair
Once the pump is repaired and normal operation is restored, your tank solids are at a healthy level (about 23% of tank volume). Continue to keep non-biodegradable materials out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and harsh chemicals all slow treatment and increase maintenance costs. Normal household use and routine maintenance will keep the system running reliably.
